Vivek —

I pulled their redlines and started a tracker (redline_tracker.xlsx). Initial take:
- SLA credit cap: they want a 20% annualized credit cap; our standard is 50% in the most severe cases. Recommend we propose a middle ground at 35% with a performance SLA tier (if we miss P99 by X ms, different remedy).
- Retention: they want 30 days for logs only — ok to accept if we carve out KV cache and training‑use logs (we should be explicit).
- Indemnity: their redline tries to broaden remedies to third‑party IP claims against us; red flags. Need Laura’s legal read here.

I’ll upload the tracker to the shared drive and populate rows by priority. Suggest a 30‑minute legal + sales sync tomorrow at 10am PT to agree negotiation posture.

All —

I reviewed StrataCore’s MSA redline. High‑level recommendations and proposed language:

1) Indemnity: Their broadened IP clause is asymmetric. We should propose the following compromise language: Redwood indemnifies for claims arising from our model outputs to the extent caused by blatant negligence or willful misconduct; for third‑party IP claims tied to customer prompts, propose limited notice/defense obligations and a cap aligned with paid fees.

2) SLA credits: Accept a reduced cap but tie credits to clearly defined SLOs and a two‑tier remediation path. Proposed cap: 35% per rolling 12‑month period.

3) Data retention & logs: Accept 30 days for diagnostic logs, excluding LLRT (low‑latency runtime cache) and ephemeral KV caches; include a clause that we delete customer prompt content per the agreed retention policy unless customer opts into extended retention.

4) Misc: Add explicit language around routing/fallback — they redlined guardrails around fallback to lower‑cost model variants; we can accommodate with an operational runbook and an SLA exception process.

I will produce an edited MSA with tracked changes and a short issue matrix (blocking / negotiable / note). Can have that to you by EOD tomorrow. If Olivia wants live negotiation, I can join a call with their counsel.

—Laura Bennett
